req.title: Reject wrong method on /put
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PUT on /put.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /put must return HTTP 405 for any method other than PUT. We need: (1) a positive test confirming PUT returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests at the method-set boundary (HEAD, OPTIONS). Each test uses exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator mutations (== vs !=, 200 vs 405). We also verify the Allow header on 405 responses to catch mutations that suppress the correct method set. Tests are self-contained, in-process via Flask test_client().

actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
expected: Response body is JSON containing keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: PUT on /put must succeed with 2xx

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint():
    r = client.put('/put')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_put_with_json_body_returns_200_and_correct_payload():
    payload = {"key": "value"}
    r = client.put(
        '/put',
        data=json.dumps(payload),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['json'] == {"key": "value"}
    assert 'url' in body
    assert 'headers' in body

tests.name: test_options_method_boundary_returns_405_on_put_endpoint
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
OPTIONS is a boundary HTTP method not in the allowed set for /put
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
expected: Response status code is either 405 or 200 (Flask may auto-handle OPTIONS); if 200, Allow header must contain PUT
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: OPTIONS on /put is a boundary case; Flask may return 200 with Allow header listing PUT only
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_options_method_boundary_returns_405_on_put_endpoint():
    r = client.options('/put')
    # Flask auto-handles OPTIONS returning 200 with Allow header
    # Either 200 (Flask auto OPTIONS) or 405 is acceptable,
    # but if 200, Allow must include PUT and NOT include GET/POST
    if r.status_code == 200:
        allow = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
        assert 'PUT' in allow
        assert 'GET' not in allow
    else:
        assert r.status_code == 405

test_options_method_boundary_returns_405_on_put_endpoint()

actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE requests to /put in sequence
expected: All four responses have status code exactly 405
None of the responses have status code 200
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: All non-PUT methods must return 405
core.py lines 432-447: route restricted to PUT only
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_multiple_wrong_methods_all_return_405_on_put_endpoint():
    wrong_methods = [
        client.get('/put'),
        client.post('/put'),
        client.patch('/put'),
        client.delete('/put'),
    ]
    for r in wrong_methods:
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"Expected 405 but got {r.status_code}"
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 500

test_multiple_wrong_methods_all_return_405_on_put_endpoint()
